Position Title: Controls Engineer

Department: Engineering

Location: UK

Position Summary
The Controls Engineer will lead the implementation of BESS (Battery Energy Storage Systems) capable of ultra-fast response to dispatch commands and grid supply variations. This candidate must be familiar with power systems, utility generation, protection, and transmission systems, as well as modern industrial networks and utility communication protocols.

What You'll Be Doing as a Controls Engineer

• Review project contracts and vendor agreements for controls-related requirements and ensure alignment throughout project execution.

• Review and validate project design packages, including electrical drawings, data flow diagrams, network designs, signal mappings (analog, Modbus, DNP3), electrical power models, and control narratives.

• Maintain and organize technical documentation within SharePoint while coordinating documentation flow with vendors and project stakeholders.

• Develop batch scripts and automation tools to streamline data collection and improve operational efficiency.

• Serve as a key technical resource for customers, EPCs, utilities, equipment vendors, and internal project teams throughout project execution.

• Troubleshoot network and communications issues within VPN-secured environments.

• Respond to customer and operator requests regarding system modifications, troubleshooting, and control system enhancements.

• Support site commissioning activities and provide technical expertise for all controls-related tasks.

• Ensure all activities are performed in compliance with engineering standards, project requirements, safety protocols, and company policies.

What You'll Bring to The Position

• Educational background in Controls Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline.

• Minimum of 3 years of experience working with industrial control systems within electrical generation, renewable energy, or similar power system environments is required.

• Experience working with inverter-based resources (IBR) such as Battery Energy Storage Systems, solar, or other renewable generation technologies

• Exposure to substations, protective relays, and transformers is preferred.

• Demonstrated experience with industrial communication protocols including Modbus, DNP3, and TCP/IP.

• Strong understanding of industrial networking, including IP addressing, subnetting, switches, firewalls, VPNs, and network communications.

• Experience with SCADA systems, plant control systems, or utility-scale automation.

• Excellent communication and problem-solving skills with the ability to collaborate across multidisciplinary teams.

• Ability to travel up to 10–15% nationally and internationally to support project sites and vendor facilities.

Canadian Solar offers a competitive salary plus fully comprehensive benefits and performance bonus package based on an annual objective achievement. Our generous benefits package includes a 401(k) Retirement Plan, medical/dental/life/disability program, vacation, and sick days.

Technicians adhere to standard operating procedures (SOPs), regulatory standards (e.g., ISO), and customer specifications to maintain consistent product quality.

Core Responsibilities:

• Adhere to SOPs, safety protocols, regulatory requirements (ISO 9001), and the company’s quality/environmental policies.

Specialized Responsibilities by Area

• Inspect incoming raw materials (e.g., silicon wafers, chemicals) to ensure they meet purchase orders and quality standards.

• Reject non-conforming materials and work with suppliers/procurement to resolve issues.

• Track records of incoming quality, including pass/fail rates and supplier performance.

2. Outgoing Quality Control (OQC) Technician

• Perform final checks on finished product batches to confirm they meet customer and internal standards.

• Test sample cells (e.g., efficiency, EL/PL imaging) from each production lot.

• Verify product packaging, labels, and shipping documents.

• Approve/reject batches based on results; escalate problematic lots to the QC Supervisor.

• Create quality reports for customers or internal teams.

• Conduct routine checks to ensure equipment accuracy and compliance with ISO 17025.

• Troubleshoot malfunctions and coordinate repairs with maintenance or vendors.

• Document calibration records and train others on proper tool use.

• Monitor solar cell production at key stages.

• Collect real-time process data and compare it to specifications.

• Alert production teams to deviations and help adjust processes to prevent defects.

• Track yield rates and identify defect trends at specific manufacturing step.

Acts as the regional senior technical specialist for power systems and product commissioning across the UK BESS fleet. This role leads product commissioning of e-STORAGE products: commissioning of e-STORAGE power conversion and MV equipment to OEM standard, including first power-on initialization parameters, product-level testing, and return-to-service. Control of work and HV authorisation are determined by contract and project phase:

• During commissioning, the EPC (or Principal Contractor) is responsible for site control of work and HV authorisation. This role operates within the EPC's safe system of work and provides product-level expertise.

• Where a third party holds HV authorisation for a site, this role coordinates, supervises interfaces, and delivers the product-level technical work within their control regime.

Key Responsibilities

Product Commissioning (e-STORAGE products)

• Lead product commissioning of e-STORAGE products across UK LTSA sites (SolBank, string inverters, MVSkids and associated MV plant) to OEM standard and project scope.

• Own and set first power-on initialization parameters (OEM-trained personnel requirement per product manuals); incorrect settings risk equipment damage and certification non-compliance.

• Own product commissioning standards, procedures, test records, and documentation packs; ensure consistency across all UK projects.

• Provide product-level technical support to the site Cx team during energisation.

• Support the site Cx team during SAT and witness testing; provide product-level technical sign-off.

HV/MV Operations & Safety

• Competent for appointment to carry out MV/HV isolations, earthing, and safety document duties under the prevailing site safe system of work, as a mandatory precursor to intrusive PM/CM works. Site HV authorisation arrangements are defined per contract and phase (see MV/HV Authorisation & Control of Work).

• Carry out operational HV/MV switching during the service phase, including switching for planned PM outages, CM interventions, and restoration on return to service, where CSE holds control of work under the contract.

• Provide HV/MV support to the service team during PM and CM activities: isolations, earthing, switching, and safe access where service team work interfaces with HV/MV plant.

• Lead HV/MV preventative maintenance across CSE, SMA and Power Electronics MV skids, RMUs, transformers, and protection systems per OEM schedules.

• Lead corrective maintenance and fault investigation on HV/MV equipment: root cause analysis, rectification and return to service.

• Provide safety leadership and oversight for all HV/MV activities in region, including supervision of third-party HV contractors where used.

Technical Expertise & Capability Building

• Subject-matter expert across all inverter platforms (CSE string inverters, SMA, Power Electronics) for HV/MV maintenance activities; product commissioning expertise applies to e-STORAGE products.

• Assess and develop service team competency for HV/MV support roles; deliver toolbox talks, training, and authorisation recommendations.

• Feed field learnings back into standards, RAMS/SOPs, and OEM escalations.

Out of Scope

• Routine non-HV/MV maintenance (LV PM, BESS enclosure servicing, HVAC, general CM). This is delivered by the regional service team, with this role providing HV oversight only where work interfaces with HV/MV plant.

• Full UK driving licence; regional and occasional national travel.
